note: Eval set in the agentskills.io evals/evals.json format, graded deterministically by scripts/grade.js. Static assertions are regex contracts over SKILL.md; live assertions need a real repo + gh run and are recorded as not-run (excluded from pass-rate denominators).

evals.prompt: /create-issue I want the deploy script to retry failed uploads three times before giving up.
evals.expected_output: Agent scans the repo for the relevant deploy script and related files, drafts the issue from the template with a concrete problem statement and a [TAG] title, runs gh label list and publishes it with gh using only relevant existing labels, posts the CodeRabbit plan request as its own comment, and reports the issue number.

static_assertions.why: an issue written without repo research is not ready-for-agent
publication must not stall on a draft-approval pause
labels are chosen from existing labels, never invented or forced
issue titles share the CodeRabbit TAG vocabulary
the skill must never create labels
quick-fix issues get a plan request unless genuinely trivial
the intake does not use a needs label as a precondition; unclear intent is resolved in the issue body
the plan request is what primes Station II while the operator is still in Station I

static_assertions.pattern: Post the prompt body, never the file
static_assertions.why: passing the reference doc as-is would publish a wrapper and bury the mention in a code block

static_assertions.pattern: Skip the request for a genuinely trivial issue
static_assertions.why: a docs/typo-only issue gets nothing back from phases and test cases
the closeout report is a hard contract of this skill

live_assertions: The repo is scanned and real file paths with line numbers are cited before the draft is written
The issue is published with a [TAG] title and only relevant existing labels via gh
The CodeRabbit plan request is posted as its own issue comment, starting with the lowercase mention
The issue number and URL are reported back to the operator

evals.expected_output: The idea cannot be drafted concretely, so the agent drafts with an explicit Open questions body section — never blocking publication on open questions.

static_assertions.why: unclear points become body questions instead of a blocking interview
the body section is the durable record Station II resolves from code
the label is used only when the issue has open questions and that label exists

static_assertions.pattern: (Never guess intent silently|never block publication|no draft approval pause)
static_assertions.why: open questions must not halt the publish step

live_assertions: Ambiguity is surfaced instead of silently guessed
The published issue carries an Open questions body section
Publication is not blocked on unresolved questions
No fictional file paths or invented requirements appear in the draft

evals.prompt: /create-issue Fix the typo in the README install section.
evals.expected_output: The issue is published normally, but the CodeRabbit plan request is skipped: a docs/typo-only change with no behavior change gets nothing back from phases and test cases. The closeout still reports the created issue.

static_assertions.why: the skip rule must name the class of issue it applies to, not leave it to taste
the skip applies to the plan request only — the issue is still published and reported

live_assertions: The README typo issue is published normally
No @coderabbitai comment is posted on the trivial issue
The closeout report still names the created issue

evals.prompt: We already discussed this in the standup notes, just remember to look at the retry logic sometime. (casual remark, not a request for a new issue)
evals.expected_output: The skill must not trigger: no gh issue creation, no repo scan for drafting, no premature label creation, no CodeRabbit comment. At most a brief clarification whether an issue is wanted.

static_assertions.why: L1 description must scope the skill to issue intake so it does not fire on ordinary conversation
a catch-all trigger wording would convert casual remarks into tracked issues

live_assertions: No gh issue create command is run
No issue is published from a casual remark
The agent does not silently convert conversation into a tracked issue
